Used by tests/conformance/test_legacy_runtime_budget.py (VAL-REGRESSION-LEGACY-BUDGET-001). Re-captured after the acef-rfc0002-incident-reporting operation (RFC-0002 v1.1 incident reporting). captured_by_feature: orchestrator re-capture after acef-rfc0002-incident-reporting M5 completion
notes: Three back-to-back warm runs with `-p no:cacheprovider` were used to suppress pytest's .pytest_cache effects. min is the conservative anchor (lowest observed; future regressions are most visible against the floor).
Headroom is 10% per VAL-REGRESSION-LEGACY-BUDGET-001. Budget check: current_seconds <= baseline_for_budget_check * 1.10.
Set ACEF_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUDGET=1 to skip the gate (e.g., on busy local machines). CI is the authoritative enforcement environment.

Lineage: pre-v0.4 19.58s/406 tests -> post-M1 (acef-v0.4-freddy-adoption) 23.345s/425 tests -> post-RFC-0002 26.87s/569 tests. The 425->569 (+144 tests) growth is the prior operation's cross-language (test_cross_lang_jcs/jws) + gzip-determinism conformance tests plus this operation's test_incident_vectors + test_incident_backward_compat.

Re-capture justification (empirical, not a number bump): per-test average runtime DROPPED across the re-capture (54.9ms/test at 425 -> 47.2ms/test at 569), so the validation hot path did not get slower per bundle. Decisive A/B under identical current load: the legacy-budget selection RESTRICTED to the pre-existing (non-newly-added) test files runs at min 24.22s vs the 23.345s post-M1 baseline = +3.7%, comfortably inside the 10% gate. The v1.1 schema-registry resolver (build_schema_registry) and per-version schema loader are both functools.lru_cache-backed, so the incident schema graph adds no per-validation rebuild cost to the v1.0 path. The +13% overage against the stale 23.345s anchor was purely added test scope (a prior operation's cross-lang/gzip tests were already inside the selector at this operation's base commit 411b65e and were never re-baselined), not a per-bundle regression.
